newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Q2 chemical output seen rising vs Q1.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Q2 chemical output seen rising vs Q1.

text.p: Mexico's chemical industry expects higher production in the second quarter than during the first three months of the year, the National Chemical Industry Association (ANIQ) said in a report.

Of 125 members surveyed in the association's quarterly poll, 87 percent of respondents forecast increased production. Fertilizer producers expect output to increase by more than 16 percent because of the agricultural cycle, the report said.
Most member chemical and petrochemical producers surveyed also expect improved domestic and export sales in the second quarter.
Overall, Mexico's chemical industry produced and exported more in the first quarter than in the first three months of the previous year, the report said.
Production of most chemicals, except for lubricants and resins, rose by more than five percent. Output of artificial and synthetic fibers rose by more than 16 percent, it said.

Of companies surveyed, 70 percent said their production had increased from the previous quarter, while 30 percent said output fell. In national sales, 67 percent said they showed an increase, while 66 percent said exports rose in the quarter.
The association's members said inflation was hurting their business and the strength of the peso was holding back exports.
